license.summary: The course is published on MIT OpenCourseWare under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and this repository (transcripts, slide transcriptions, slide images and wiki prose) is offered under the same licence. Third-party figures that OCW marks as excluded from its licence are described in prose only and never rendered into raw/images/.

figureAudit.note: All twenty-one transcribed decks were audited against the PDF by an independent reader. caveats: Covers lectures 1-21 of 24 only. The course map says which later lecture teaches a topic, but nothing here records what those lectures say.
Transcripts are OCW's human-made captions with a light copy-edit; every change is listed in the file header and the unedited text is in raw/transcripts/original/.
Lecture 1's deck labels later topics with 'Lecture N' banners that do not all match the recorded schedule (e.g. transformers 'Lecture 9', recorded as 8); wiki/course-map.md maps them.
Slides 45 and 70 of lecture 1 are animation frames clipped in OCW's PDF; their heat maps and batch matrices are not recoverable from the deck.
The lecture 1 deck's title slide reads '6.S898 Deep Learning, Fall 2022' - a reused deck, transcribed as printed.
Lecture 2's deck ends with a worked numerical backprop example (slides 72-80) that the recording does not reach; the wiki takes it from the slides alone.
Lecture 2's slide 79 misprints one multiplier (-0.1186 for -0.1869; its printed result uses the right value), and its weight-update slides use +eta with a negative learning rate; the wiki flags both.

Lecture 3's deck is handwritten (iPad notes); its PDF text layer is OCR noise and was not used. Everything was read from page images, and the equation-, diagram- and chart-heavy pages were audited by a different model.
Lecture 3's slide 30 prints KINKS_0 = 1 as the base case of its kink-counting bound; in the recording a student corrects it to 0 and the base case is left unresolved. The wiki reports both.
Lecture 3's slide 39 cites the Chinchilla paper as 'Hoffmann, Borgeau, Mensch et al (2020)'; it is transcribed as written.

Lecture 4's deck has 35 of 84 slides excluded from OCW's licence, including every figure built on the stork and heron photographs (segmentation, feature maps, receptive fields, encoder-decoder, U-net, ResNet); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 4's slide 40 prints x_out[C, :] where its 0-based indexing means C - 1, and slide 39 leaves unclear whether the bias is inside the channel sum; the lecturer calls slide 25's vertical-edge filter 'horizontal edges'. The wiki flags all three.

Lecture 5's deck has 14 of 47 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the application examples, J. Leskovec's tree-view illustrations, the two example architectures, the positional-encoding results); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 5's slide 41 plots eight training-accuracy curves but labels only three groups with arrows (sum with an MLP, sum with linear+ReLU, mean/max); per-curve values are read approximately from the plot.

Lecture 5's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 18's max aggregation lacks its closing brace, slides 40-41 drop the opening bracket after g_1, slide 30's first coefficient c^{vu} carries no r, and slide 39's h^(t) is unbolded with no node subscript.

Lecture 6's deck has 8 of 66 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the Paul the octopus article, the pix2pix and edges2cats figures, all four Belkin et al. double-descent figures, and the NeRF and polypharmacy figures); those exist here as prose descriptions only, and slide 62 is not rendered because its photograph is lecture 4's excluded heron image.

Lecture 6's slides 10-11 print n = 30, m = 10 for a 30-fruit vocabulary and 10-fruit lists (the reverse of slide 9's definitions), and slide 10's s = 100 trillion matches neither 10^30 nor 30^10; the wiki reports the numbers without resolving them.
Lecture 6's slides 41 and 43 call the number of dichotomies the 'VC dimension'; the wiki follows the slides, with one note marked as outside the course material that textbook usage differs.

Lecture 7's deck is handwritten (iPad notes), like lecture 3's; its text layer is OCR noise and was not used except for OCW's typed notices. 3 of its 32 slides (7, 25, 26) carry Keller Jordan's plots, which OCW excludes from its licence; they exist here as prose descriptions only, including slides 25 and 26's handwritten width claim and depth recipe.

Lecture 7's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 11's boxed Newton step drops the lambda of the line above it, slides 13-15 write the Gauss-Newton product with no transpose, slide 19 says 'right had side' and prints the dual formulation of steepest descent with no minus sign (problem set 2's version has one).

In lecture 7's recording the lecturer says (1 + x/L^2)^L tends to 0; the wiki reports it with one note marked as outside the course material that the limit is 1. He also says depth increases 'as I go down' the curves of slide 7's depth plot, the reverse of the plot; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 8's deck has 7 of 55 slides excluded from OCW's licence (Fredo Durand's bird photograph on slides 4 and 6-8, the DINO attention maps, the ScaleMAE figure, and the 'Attention Is All You Need' figure); those exist here as prose descriptions only. Its outline slide is headed '9. Transformers' although the title slide and recording are lecture 8.

Lecture 8's slide 29 prints key-query scores (1, 0.2, 0.9, 0.1) that do not match its attention weights (0.1, 0.2, 1, 0.1), which do not sum to 1; the lecturer calls the first score a typo for 0.1. Its slide 39 pseudocode reuses K for the patch size and the key matrix and divides by sqrt(d) outside the softmax, where slide 34 divides inside; slide 34 scales by sqrt(m) while its diagram labels the dimension M. The wiki reports each as printed.

In lecture 8's recording the lecturer says attention is 'permutation invariant' where slide 41 says equivariant, and that layer norm divides 'by the variance' where slide 38 divides by its square root; the wiki gives both.

Lecture 9's deck has 21 of 72 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the chest X-ray, the coffee-cup loading example, the augmentation photographs, the domain-randomization images and OpenAI's robot-hand results, the Stable Diffusion and AlphaFold screenshots, every colorization photograph, a facade-generation grid, and the Weights & Biases, spice-rack and Scale ML screenshots); those exist here as prose descriptions only.

Lecture 9's recording runs out of time after the model section: most of the optimization, evaluation, debugging and compute slides (48-71) are never spoken, and the wiki takes them from the slides alone.

In lecture 9's recording the lecturer describes slide 4's DeGrave, Janizek and Lee example as a breast-cancer (benign or malignant) classifier; the slide shows a chest X-ray and names no disease. The wiki gives both, with one note marked as outside the course material that the cited paper concerns COVID-19 detection from chest radiographs.

Lecture 9's slides print small slips, transcribed as written and flagged: slide 10's layernorm mean carries 1/k in front of a sum over k, slide 30's argmin formula has unbalanced parentheses, and slide 70 writes torch.cudnn.benchmark (the wiki adds one note marked as outside the course material that PyTorch's flag is torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark).

Lecture 10's deck has 20 of 69 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the classroom video frame, the video strip, audio waveform, space-time cube and its slices, the photographs of the lecturer's cat Frank, which OCW marks '© source unknown', and the Reformer and Longformer figures); those exist here as prose descriptions only. Its outline slides are headed '11. Memory and sequence modeling' (slides 2 and 67) and '9. Memory and sequence modeling' (slide 68) although the title slide and recording are lecture 10.

Lecture 10's LSTM slides (33-39) are derived from Chris Olah's blog post and use its plain notation (x_t, h_t, C_t), not the bold notation of the rest of the deck; the wiki follows each slide's notation.

In lecture 10's recording the lecturer calls the hidden-to-hidden weights 'v' where slide 23 has W, calls the powers of W 'quadratic' before calling them exponential, says 'maximizing cross-entropy' where slide 50 says minimize, and describes byte pairs as two-character pairs, about 26 times 26 of them (lecture 8 has a byte pair for 'I-N-G'); the transcript marks the first three and the wiki gives each beside the slide.

Lecture 11's deck has 22 of 65 slides excluded from OCW's licence (the car, fish and bird photographs used throughout, Serre's visual-cortex diagram, Zeiler and Fergus's patch mosaics, the colorization photographs, the conv5 stimulus grid and Yann LeCun's cake slide); those exist here as prose descriptions only, and slide 13 is not rendered because its CLIP figure is lecture 1's excluded slide 73 figure. Its outline slide is headed '12. Representation Learning I' although the title slide and recording are lecture 11.

Lecture 11's slide 9 prints the softmax with a minus sign in the exponent, e^{-tau x}, and its wiring-graph node without the tau; slide 60 cites the masked-autoencoder paper ([He, Chen, Xie, et al. 2021]) for BERT; slides 25-28 print 'Neural' where 'Neutral' is meant. The slide file transcribes each as printed, and the wiki gives slide 9's formula as printed.

In lecture 11's recording the lecturer works the linear-autoencoder-equals-PCA derivation from equations that are not in the OCW deck (slide 41 prints only the conclusion); the wiki gives the argument in his words without reconstructing the equations. He calls k-means' optimizer expectation maximization where slide 48 says block coordinate descent, and assigns the coloured-shapes experiments to 'p set 3' where OCW has them in Homework 4; the wiki gives both.
